title: Authority-Indexed Reaction Algebra for ZRM
goal: Derive and test a compositional, proof-relevant authority semantics that refines ARM-style private resource proofs into ZRM state-transition authority without losing exact fact use, integer conservation laws, context freshness, or commit boundaries.

sources.title: A Compositional Framework for Reaction Networks
sources.authors: John C. Baez; Blake S. Pollard
sources.relevance: Treats open reaction networks as composable morphisms and separates internal reaction structure from boundary behavior.
sources.limitation: Does not model authorization capabilities, exact fact use, adversarial proof inputs, or durable commit.

sources.title: Open Petri Nets
sources.relevance: Provides compositional open Petri-net semantics and a categorical account of gluing process boundaries.
sources.limitation: Ordinary token-flow semantics is proof-irrelevant and does not distinguish authority witnesses with equal incidence vectors.

sources.title: Resources, Concurrency and Local Reasoning
sources.relevance: Motivates separating resources and composing independent computations through local reasoning.
sources.limitation: Heap separation alone does not provide policy-version, proof-release, or affine-capability semantics.

sources.title: Views: Compositional Reasoning for Concurrent Programs
sources.authors: Thomas Dinsdale-Young; Lars Birkedal; Philippa Gardner; Matthew Parkinson; Hongseok Yang
sources.relevance: Abstracts compositional concurrency reasoning over resource/view structures rather than one fixed heap model.
sources.limitation: Does not by itself define exact proof-coverage or cryptographic authority.

sources.title: Iris: Monoids and Invariants as an Orthogonal Basis for Concurrent Reasoning
sources.relevance: Uses resource algebras and invariants to represent authoritative and fragmentary ownership in a compositional logic.
sources.limitation: AIRA must define concrete ZRM authority objects and cannot inherit Iris soundness without a formal embedding.

sources.title: Provenance Semirings
sources.authors: Todd J. Green; Gregory Karvounarakis; Val Tannen
sources.relevance: Shows that algebraic provenance can retain which inputs contribute to an output rather than only the output value.
sources.limitation: Database derivation provenance is not automatically affine authorization or exact-once state authority.

sources.title: Provenance Traces
sources.authors: James Cheney; Umut A. Acar; Amal Ahmed
sources.relevance: Makes execution dependence explicit through replayable traces and supports reasoning about provenance correctness.
sources.limitation: Trace correctness does not establish policy freshness or durable state commit.

sources.title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
sources.authors: Arnar Birgisson; Joe Gibbs Politz; Ulfar Erlingsson; Ankur Taly; Michael Vrable
sources.relevance: Demonstrates context-bound attenuation and explicit caveats for delegated authority.
sources.limitation: Macaroon validation is not a typed resource-conservation or commit semantics.

sources.title: SecPAL: Design and Semantics of a Decentralized Authorization Language
sources.authors: Moritz Y. Becker; Cedric Fournet; Andrew D. Gordon
sources.relevance: Separates declarative authorization policy from application code and gives deterministic policy semantics.
sources.limitation: It does not define shielded resource accounting, recursive proof aggregation, or storage linearization.

sources.title: Linearizability: A Correctness Condition for Concurrent Objects
sources.authors: Maurice P. Herlihy; Jeannette M. Wing
sources.relevance: Requires a concurrent implementation to refine an explicit sequential object and identifies operation linearization points.
sources.limitation: Linearizability does not determine the semantic validity of a resource transition before commit.

sources.title: Partial-Order Methods for the Verification of Concurrent Systems
sources.relevance: Formalizes independence-based reduction of interleavings and motivates schedule-independent semantic identity.
sources.limitation: Independence must include facts, resources, policy context, and authenticated footprints, not only memory actions.

sources.title: Unfolding-Based Partial Order Reduction
sources.authors: Cesar Rodriguez; Marcelo Sousa; Subodh Sharma; Daniel Kroening
sources.relevance: Uses event structures and unfolding to avoid redundant interleavings while preserving concurrency behavior.
sources.limitation: AIRA requires an authority-aware dependence relation and separate proof-topology identity.

sources.title: Convex Integer Maximization via Graver Bases
sources.authors: Jesus A. De Loera; Raymond Hemmecke; Shmuel Onn; Robert Weismantel
sources.relevance: Uses primitive integer-kernel directions as universal augmentation moves and motivates minimal witness-collision generators.
sources.limitation: General Graver-basis computation can be expensive; bounded enumeration is only research evidence.

sources.title: Graver Bases and Universal Groebner Bases for Linear Codes
sources.relevance: Relates primitive lattice relations, toric ideals, and canonical algebraic generating sets.
sources.limitation: The code/ideal setting does not itself establish authority semantics.

sources.title: Fast Computation of the Smith Normal Form with Multipliers for a Nonsingular Integer Matrix
sources.authors: George Birmpilis; George Labahn; Arne Storjohann
sources.relevance: Studies exact Smith form with transformation multipliers, useful for replayable lattice certificates and torsion detection.
sources.limitation: A deterministic software decomposition is profile-bound; the multipliers are not a unique mathematical normal form.

sources.title: Markov Bases: A 25 Year Update
sources.relevance: Surveys integer fibers and moves connecting witnesses with the same sufficient statistic.
sources.limitation: Statistical fiber connectivity is not the same as safe capability reuse.

sources.title: The Update Framework: Survivable Key Compromise in Software Update Systems
sources.authors: Justin Cappos; Justin Samuel; Scott Baker; John H. Hartman
sources.relevance: Separates roles, freshness, consistency, expiry, and revocation in a governed security metadata system.
sources.limitation: Software-update metadata is not a general resource-machine semantics.

sources.title: A Framework for Compositional Verification of Security Protocols
sources.relevance: Emphasizes explicit assumptions and compositional proof obligations across protocol components.
sources.limitation: It does not supply the concrete AIRA algebra or ZRM runtime boundary.

sources.title: The Calculus of Computation
sources.relevance: Provides SMT-oriented invariant and transition-system reasoning used by bounded semantic oracles.
sources.limitation: Solver success remains conditional on the correctness of the model and translation.

sources.title: A Formally Verified Checker for Proofs of Unsatisfiability
sources.relevance: Motivates small independently checked certificates rather than trusting solver or generator output directly.
sources.limitation: AIRA's current certificates are not yet exported as independently checked SAT/SMT proof objects.

sources.title: Anoma Resource Machine Specification
sources.relevance: Defines the resource-machine concepts that ARM instantiates, including resources, commitments, nullifiers, logics, and deltas.
sources.limitation: The specification does not by itself provide ZRM's governed fact and exact-once commit architecture.

sources.title: Anoma RISC Zero Resource Machine
sources.relevance: Provides a concrete shielded resource, compliance, logic-proof, delta, and RISC Zero aggregation implementation.
sources.limitation: Repository behavior is revision-specific and proof validity remains distinct from policy authority and durable commit.

sources.title: The Iris 3.5 Reference
sources.relevance: Documents cameras/resource algebras, authoritative ownership, and invariants used as a comparison point for AIRA capabilities.
sources.limitation: AIRA is not an Iris model until a formal interpretation is supplied.

sources.title: Categories for the Working Mathematician
sources.relevance: Supplies the categorical language needed to state indexed composition, monoidal structure, and coherence obligations precisely.
sources.limitation: Category-theoretic terminology does not replace executable semantics or proofs.

hypotheses.claim: Net typed effect alone is insufficient to reconstruct authority use when the reaction map has a nontrivial integer kernel.
hypotheses.test: Find two nonnegative reaction witnesses with the same boundary effect but different exact fact manifests.

hypotheses.claim: A Smith-decomposition-derived cycle grade of dimension equal to reaction nullity makes effect-plus-grade injective over the full integer witness group.
hypotheses.test: Check S*A*T=D, derive the tail rows of T inverse, prove grade times kernel basis is identity, and search for bounded collisions.

hypotheses.claim: The minimum dimension of any globally injective linear authority grade is the integer reaction nullity.
hypotheses.test: Prove the lower bound by rank-nullity after tensoring with Q and exhibit a nullity-dimensional construction.

hypotheses.claim: Primitive conformal integer-kernel relations generate high-value adversarial pairs of nonnegative authority witnesses with equal typed effect.
hypotheses.test: Enumerate bounded kernel vectors, retain conformally indecomposable relations, split positive and negative parts, and replay equal effects.

hypotheses.claim: Integer torsion in the cokernel captures lot-size and modular reachability restrictions invisible to rational rank.
hypotheses.test: Use boundary [2], verify full rational rank but Smith factor 2, and reject odd effects.

hypotheses.claim: Exact proof coverage has at least two semantically distinct profiles: separable capacities reducible to integral max-flow and indivisible bundles requiring exact set partition or SAT.
hypotheses.test: Construct one instance where splitting a bundle would accept an invalid coverage and verify profile-specific solvers.

hypotheses.claim: A failed separable-coverage attempt can return a replayable max-flow/min-cut deficit certificate instead of an opaque rejection.
hypotheses.test: Verify flow feasibility, conservation, cut capacity, and unmet claim demand independently.

hypotheses.claim: Authority facts form a capacity-bounded partial commutative resource algebra rather than an unrestricted commutative monoid.
hypotheses.test: Prove valid disjoint uses compose, while duplicate affine use or capacity overflow is undefined and rejected.

hypotheses.claim: Parallel semantic identity should be invariant under presentation order only when authenticated resource, fact, and footprint independence all hold.
hypotheses.test: Generate independent shards in both orders and compare roots; introduce each conflict class and require rejection.

hypotheses.claim: A canonical dependency DAG can define schedule-independent transition identity while proof-tree topology remains a separate identity.
hypotheses.test: Enumerate linear extensions of one dependency DAG and show one semantic root but multiple proof topology roots.

hypotheses.claim: Moving a shard across a policy or verifier context requires an explicit governed context morphism; equality of application-level effects is insufficient.
hypotheses.test: Substitute policy snapshot, validation context, verifier release, basis, or schema root and require rejection absent an approved transport certificate.

hypotheses.claim: A total semantic delta carrier must admit the additive identity; nonzero ECDSA signing-key wrappers are unsuitable as the semantic composition carrier.
hypotheses.test: Exhibit nonzero scalars a and -a whose sum is zero and a parenthesization whose intermediate representability differs.

hypotheses.claim: A proof that commits to a caller-supplied kind table proves self-consistency, not that the table is the governed accounting basis.
hypotheses.test: Compare self-committed substituted table acceptance with exact expected-root and derivation-profile binding.

hypotheses.claim: ARM-style private group accounting can refine ZRM typed rows only under an explicit computational basis-binding assumption and exact governed statement binding.
hypotheses.test: State the binding assumption explicitly, prove the symbolic refinement conditionally, and search for known-relation countermodels.

hypotheses.claim: Proof validity can authorize only a pure ZRM commit plan; it cannot establish freshness at the linearization point or durable commit success.
hypotheses.test: Model a valid proof followed by a stale-state race and require conflict-with-no-write rather than accepted journal.

hypotheses.claim: The combined AIRA structure is best modeled as an indexed partial double-resource structure: tensor for independent shards, ordered composition for state continuity, and explicit vertical context transport.
hypotheses.test: Prove units and associativity on defined operations, an interchange law under independence, and functorial identity/composition for context transport.
